thread:
ravi (finance): ParityMeter renewal review 023 quote looks clean but the SKU table is ambiguous about streaming/session billing and telemetry. Can procurement + eng list clarifying questions before I sign?
megan (procurement): I noticed line items that look like both "per-call" and "per-event" charging for the same traffic. Need canonical mapping to our consumption buckets: non-stream gen, streaming chat, embeddings batch.
diego (eng-ml): Their docs say "billing per request or per-segment" which is vague for websocket streaming. Ask for explicit worked examples.
ravi (finance): Redacted SKU snippet:
```
SKU,Unit,Price,Notes
PM-TOK,token,0.00048,standard per-token
PM-EMB,embedding,0.0019,per-embedding-unit
PM-EVENT,event,0.00002,telemetry/ingress-event
PM-SEG,segment,0.005,per-stream-segment
PM-RESERVE,monthly,2500,reserved credits + discount
```
megan (procurement): Key asks: whether PM-SEG applies in addition to PM-TOK for streaming; whether PM-EVENT fires on every token or per-request header; proration rules if we change reserved tier mid-month; and reserved credit rollover policy.
clare (legal): Contract needs: 30-day dispute window, auditable usage with right to export raw logs, and clear invoice reconciliation SLA. Their standard 7-day dispute is too short.
yuri (security): Security: what telemetry contains (do logs include prompt or response text), retention windows, and whether they support in-flight redaction or KMS-backed storage. Also where data is hosted (US/EU).
diego (eng-ml): For reconciliation we'll need a raw export that includes: request_id, utc_ts, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, segment_count, embedding_units, sku_applied, cost_usd. Ask for BigQuery export + daily CSV.
paritymeter-bot: ParityMeter AE: "Thanks for the questions. We'll provide: 1) canonical SKU mapping with three worked examples (single completion, streaming 12-turn chat, batch 200k embeddings), 2) sample invoice PDF and the CSV row mapping, 3) BigQuery raw export + daily CSV, 4) confirmation that PM-SEG (segment) is waived for reserved customers or can be disabled, 5) SOC2 Type II and SAML support, 6) adjustable log retention (30/90/365) and optional KMS redaction, 7) proration rules and reserved credit rollover (up to 2 months). We'll attach samples in reply"
megan (procurement): Good. I'll consolidate and ask them to show the math line-by-line for the three scenarios and include the exact CSV row that would generate each invoice line.
ravi (finance): Priority: High = SKU mapping + BigQuery export + sample invoice. Medium = proration/rollover & dispute terms. Low = residency details.
clare (legal): I'll draft the redline for audit/dispute and circulate once we have the sample invoice.
yuri (security): I'll follow up on KMS scope and whether redaction is automatic or manual.
megan (procurement): I'll send the consolidated list to the AE after a last pass. Ping me if you want additional items.
